name: PREREG_router_screen_v1
question: On a small synthetic fixed screen task, does the 0.4.0 router kit reproduce the v2.1/v2.2 router logic: fast scripted actions in the learned state, hand-over on unseen screens, every wrong fast action caught at the next observation, the sealed trigger firing on a redesign, and a relearning cycle that restores the learned-state level?

conditions.router: SimThink D screen-state decider (ScreenAdapter: 8x6 colour grid + window title + previous action) + SkillTable learned from teacher transitions (expected next states); fast action only if p >= tau, the state has a skill and it is an expected next state; else the stub large model
conditions.negative_wrong_expectation: same as router, with the PROFILE skill expecting LOGIN (deliberately wrong)
conditions.negative_wrong_action: same as router, with the LOGIN skill doing SUBMIT (deliberately wrong action)

tasks.T: sign in, save a profile form, close 0-2 error dialogs and save again (examples/router_screen/screens.py)

large_model: stub: reads the app's true screen and applies screens.POLICY; no network; counted as one call per hand-over
teacher: stub: the app's true screen state (screens outside the task are skipped)
pilot_seeds: 9001-9510 (unsealed pilot of the code paths only)
perturb_note: as v2.1: banner (covers the save button once) and session (expired page after the first action) never appear in training
tau_source: same as v2.1 and v2.2, fixed a priori
trigger_source: same as v2.2, fixed a priori
success: the app's final state is DONE with no overlay and no duplicate save, and the run stopped there (execution-verified)
metrics: wrong fast actions: caught at the next route (any hand-over / by no-progress), not caught, wrong final
teacher calls, relearn training seconds, old and new weight hashes
route ms p50/p95 (not in the digest)

hypotheses.H1: learned state, clean runs (perturb none): success = all, hand-over rate <= 0.20
hypotheses.H2: learned state, unseen disturbances (banner, session): success >= 0.9 of those runs, false stops = 0
hypotheses.H3: every wrong non-final fast action in the learned and both negative conditions is followed by a hand-over at the next route (fast_wrong_not_caught = 0)
hypotheses.H4: negative_wrong_expectation: at least one no-progress hand-over per run; negative_wrong_action: every run has at least one wrong fast action and all of them are caught by no-progress
hypotheses.H5: redesign: the trigger fires during the detect runs
hypotheses.H6: after relearning on the redesign: success = all, hand-over rate <= learned-state clean hand-over rate + 0.10
hypotheses.H7: layout A after relearning: success = all (no forgetting)
hypotheses.H8: a second run on the same machine gives the same digest

stop_rule: results reported as measured; no re-run with changed tau, trigger or criteria under this PREREG; failed hypotheses are reported as failed
safety: local Python process only; no browser, no network, no large-model calls
